jobs.description:
Position: Environmental Compliance Associate (Full Time)

Environmental.com (EDC) is seeking an Environmental Compliance Associate to join our team in providing environmental compliance solutions to clients across California.

**Qualifications:**

· Bachelor’s Degree - required

· Qualified Industrial Stormwater Practitioner (QISP) Certification – preferred

o Ability to obtain certification within 3 months of hiring

· Experience in stormwater, wastewater, drinking water, hazardous waste, air, or solid waste (1 year) – strongly preferred

· Valid California Driver’s License - required

Duties will include but not limited to:

· Preparing and amending Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs), including stormwater site maps

· Conducting fieldwork which includes site visits, audits, inspections, sampling, monitoring, pollutant source assessments, and training

· Tracking of data and monitoring activities

· Providing technical expertise regarding the Industrial General Permit (IGP), stormwater, and appropriate Best Management Practices (BMPs)

· Writing regulatory reports and correspondence with a variety of stakeholders

· Developing monitoring plans in accordance with individual and local environmental permits and regulations

· Assisting in environmental compliance projects (planning, monitoring, and reporting)

· Recruit clients (existing and new) for additional services

**The ideal candidate should be able to demonstrate:**

· Ability to comprehend and interpret Local, State, and Federal stormwater regulations (other environmental focuses are a bonus)

· Strong interpersonal and communication (written and verbal) skills with a great attention to detail

· Strong project management skills

· Ability to work independently and collaboratively with other members

· Ability to analyze data and prepare reports

· Proficiency with Microsoft Office Tools (Outlook, Word, Excel, Power Point)

Job Type: Full-time

Pay: $50,000.00 - $55,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan

Ability to Commute:

* Signal Hill, CA 90755 (Required)

Work Location: In person

### **Job Description and Duties**

This position offers an exciting and rewarding opportunity to be part of a team of interdisciplinary scientists in the Aquatic Ecology Unit (AEU) and the Interagency Ecological Program (IEP). AEU conducts long-term monitoring and aquatic ecology field studies in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta. The incumbent is responsible for leading field surveys for the collection of fisheries, invertebrate, water quality, and other ecological data for the Yolo Bypass Fish Monitoring Program, affiliated special studies, and other long-term IEP monitoring programs. The incumbent will correctly identify and monitor native and non-native fish and lower trophic communities using a variety of techniques, including use of a rotary screw trap, fyke trap, net tows, and beach seine surveys. Other duties include but are not limited to laboratory processing of water quality, biological, and molecular samples, implementing new quality control measures, maintaining and troubleshooting field equipment, and preparing technical data reports. Field duties require rigorous physical work under variable conditions.

  

**As a permanent-intermittent position, the incumbent may not exceed working 1,500 hours in a calendar year. Permanent-intermittent (PI) employees are eligible to receive benefits after meeting the required work hour criteria and do receive holiday pay on a pro-rated basis.**

### **Job Description and Duties**

Vegetation management and wildfire resiliency are statewide priorities. The increase in the frequency and magnitude of fires throughout the state is not only a concern for California’s residents, but for our wildlands and biological resources as well. The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has an open position which will implement a monitoring program for vegetation management projects approved under the Governor’s March 1, 2025 State of Emergency.
  
  
We want you to join our small team within the Habitat Conservation Planning Branch (Branch) located in West Sacramento. Our team works on timber harvesting and fire resiliency policy for CDFW and supports a larger, statewide program of dedicated scientists.

Here are some things that you will do:

• Assist the Timberland Conservation and Fire Resiliency Program (Program) to implement CDFW monitoring program in response to the Governor’s March 1, 2025 State of Emergency proclamation

• Coordinate with CDFW regional staff on monitoring protocols, procedures, scheduling, data, reporting, and guidance

• Collect biological data at site visits, sometimes with CDFW colleagues or staff from other departments

• Manage, analyze, and report monitoring data

• Provide fire policy and internal technical guidance support within the Program

• Participate in internal and external working groups, including Program and Branch working groups

• Collaborate on fire resiliency activities across CDFW programs and Regions, including working with other CDFW programs to incorporate the impacts of fire into biological resources planning, permitting, monitoring, and restoration

• Analyze new legislative bills about fire and biological resources

• Participate in Program strategic planning and goal setting

• Coordinate with Program staff to respond to California Board of Forestry and Fire Protection proposals

• Assist with implementation of the Governor’s California Wildfire & Forest Resilience Action Plan

• Conduct research and basic GIS analysis to support Program work

• Assist with compliance monitoring projects in coordination with CAL FIRE, the Water Boards, and the CA Geologic Survey; coordinate data collection and assist CDFW Regional Staff with fieldwork

  
This position is office-centered and currently allows for a one day per week telework hybrid option. Required in-office attendance may change based on operational need. The office building is in West Sacramento, Yolo County, with limited public transportation options but free parking available.  
  
  

**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.

  

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:

  

Personal Leave Program - Human Resources - CalHR.

  
  

This position may be eligible for a telework opportunity in accordance with departmental policies and operational needs. Beginning July 1, 2026, employees will be required to work in-person at least four (4) days per week in alignment with Executive Order N-22-25. Additional in-office days may be required based on operational needs.

  
  

In order to be eligible for this position, you must either be transfer eligible or take and pass the following exam.

  

Class Title: Environmental Scientist

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

The position is office-centered and requires the use of a computer for several hours each day; the completion of office tasks that require sitting, standing, and walking to other locations; and attendance at in-person meetings and participation in conference calls. In-person participation in meetings, training, and outreach events will be prioritized over virtual options. The position may require driving a vehicle to conduct fieldwork and occasional travel up to 5%, including travel by vehicle up to eight hours to conduct fieldwork. A valid California driver’s license is required to drive to project sites and may require travel of up to three or more hours each way including overnight travel, early mornings, late nights, hiking over uneven and possibly steep or wet terrain, use of alternative methods of transportation (including all-terrain vehicle), and work in inclement weather. Travel to meetings and field sites with the use of a state vehicle may be required. The incumbent may incur overtime. The position may require the incumbent to wear a uniform identifying the employee as Department staff.
